settings.rulesFailuresHint: Links you pasted that no rule could resolve are grouped by domain here, keeping the last error and a failure count — use this list when writing a rule pack for those sites. Resolved links are dropped automatically; the ledger stays on this machine.

screencast.title: Screen Cast
screencast.noDevice: No online device found, refresh the list first
screencast.screenTip: With multiple displays, cast just one: "Full Screen" grabs the union of all monitors — squeezed image, higher bitrate, and older TVs may fail to decode it.
screencast.screenTipWayland: Under Wayland the screen-copy protocol hands over one output at a time, so there is no "union of all monitors": "Full Screen" casts the primary display. Pick another entry above to cast a different one.
screencast.windowTip: The list holds the windows currently on screen; capture grabs that region of the screen, so any window on top of the one you pick is what the TV will show — keep the chosen window in front. Re-pick after the window moves, closes, or minimizes. On macOS without Screen Recording permission titles show as "(untitled)", so only the owner app identifies them.
screencast.noMicLinux: No microphone input source found (PipeWire/PulseAudio reports no recording source). Either the pactl command is missing on this machine, or this sound card's input port is disabled — check pavucontrol → Input Devices.
screencast.micAsking: Requesting microphone access — tap "Allow" in the system dialog…
screencast.micDenied: Microphone access is still denied, so the cast would be silent. Allow HanCast in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, then retry.
screencast.noSystemSound: No system audio device detected (macOS 14.2+: HanCast creates "HanCast 系统声音" automatically; macOS 14.1 or older needs BlackHole; Windows needs Stereo Mix or a WASAPI loopback)
screencast.noSystemSoundLinux: No system-sound mirror source found (PipeWire's <output>.monitor for each output). Most likely this machine has no pactl command — installing either pipewire-pulse or pulseaudio is enough; plain ALSA cannot capture system sound.
screencast.loopbackTip: On Windows every output device has its own loopback mirror, and only the mirror of the current default output actually carries sound; pick an idle one and the picture is fine but the cast is silent. After switching output devices (unplugging headphones, pairing Bluetooth) close this panel and reopen it to refresh the list.
screencast.loopbackTipLinux: On Linux every output has its own mirror source (PipeWire's <output>.monitor), and only the one marked "playing now" actually carries sound; pick an idle output and the picture is fine but the cast is silent. After switching output devices (unplugging headphones, pairing Bluetooth) close this panel and reopen it to refresh the list.
screencast.inviteLink: Invite link (watch in browser, no install)
screencast.inviteTip: Open this link on your LAN to watch. Up to 20 viewers.
screencast.dlnaTip: Streaming to TV via DLNA. Picture may take a few seconds (live latency is normal).
screencast.ffmpegMissing: FFmpeg not found, screen casting unavailable
screencast.wlgrabMissing: This is a Wayland session but the bundled capture helper hancast-wlgrab is unavailable — a cast started now would be pure black (x11grab cannot see Wayland windows).
screencast.wlgrabHint: Wayland desktops such as Hyprland / Sway must capture the screen through the wlroots screen-copy protocol; FFmpeg has no such input. Check that the installed package's resources contain hancast-wlgrab, or point HANCAST_WLGRAB at a working binary.

logs.title: Runtime Logs
logs.hint: For troubleshooting: pick a module and level, then Refresh. Turn on DEBUG before reproducing the issue to capture device discovery and cast requests in full. Export saves the log file locally so you can send it to the developer.

logs.truncated: Only the newest entries are shown
devices.addSelfHint: HanCast can also act as a receiver. Add this computer to the device list to cast to itself (e.g. play full-screen on this machine, or control it from a phone).
devices.addHint: Auto discovery relies on LAN multicast, which firewalls and security software often block (that is why Windows can find the Mac but not the other way round). Enter the address directly: a device IP (e.g. 192.168.1.68), IP:port, or the full description.xml link from the device page. Added devices are remembered and reconnected on startup.
devices.addressPlaceholder: Device IP / IP:port / full description.xml URL
devices.hiddenHint: Hidden devices stay out of the list but are still discovered. Click Restore to bring one back.
devices.addFailed: Could not reach that address: check that the device is on, on the same subnet, and allows connections to its service port
screencast.noDeviceHint: No TV / big screen found? Add it by IP manually, and check both firewalls allow HanCast.
